title: The torsion bound over a weakly contractible base
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be separated schemes of finite type over $k$, the standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], let $p:X\to Y$ be a proper $k$-morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $d\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0}$ bound the Krull dimensions of all geometric fibres [def-pc-base-change, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $V\to Y$ be an affine weakly contractible object of $Y_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [sk-def-pe-weak-contractible, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and set $X_V=X\times_YV$, with projection $p_V:X_V\to V$. The scheme $V$ need not be Noetherian. Let $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ be a locally closed immersion, factor it as $S\xrightarrow{u}\overline S\xrightarrow{i}X$ with $u$ open and $i$ closed, and put $a_!=i_*u_!$ [det-lem-int-tensor-projection]. Write $\mathcal O_{E,T}=p_T^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ for the coefficient ring object pulled back from the condensed topological valuation ring [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $L_0$ be a lisse finite free $\mathcal O_{E,S}$-module, meaning a module object [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] which on a pro-étale covering is a finite direct sum of $\mathcal O_{E,S}$. For $n\ge1$ put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n$, using its finite discrete constant coefficient sheaf. Then the relative derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] has a natural isomorphism
$$
(a_!L_0)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}(A_n)_X\simeq a_!(L_0/\pi_E^nL_0).
$$
Its right-hand side is a sheaf in degree zero and is classical constructible: it is $\nu_X^*F_n$ for a constructible étale $A_n$-module sheaf $F_n$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. If $r:X_V\to X$ is the other projection and $r^*$ is finite constant-coefficient inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], then pro-étale cohomology [def-sfb-finite-derived-global-sections] satisfies
$$
H^q(X_V,r^*a_!(L_0/\pi_E^nL_0))=0\qquad(q>2d).
$$

proof.text: The generator extension is fully faithful onto modules supported on the locally closed immersion. Tensoring an extended module with a pulled-back point module keeps that support. Restrict, use the coefficient pullback isomorphism, and reconstruct; uniqueness under the fully faithful restriction proves naturality. The extension of a lisse module is flat, so the single-object tensor comparison gives the natural derived reduction isomorphism.

source.place: Torsion reduction proof, Lean implementation step 1

proof.text: Finite type over the field and quasi-compactness make X Noetherian. The closed and open subspaces are topologically Noetherian, so the open immersion is quasi-compact. Extension of scalars sends a finite direct sum of regular modules to the corresponding finite free quotient module. The quotient thus has finite constant local models, and open extension and closed pushforward preserve its finite constructible stratification.

source.place: Torsion reduction proof, Lean implementation step 2

proof.text: The ordinary scalar-extension tensor isomorphism identifies the integral tensor quotient with restriction of the module over the actual quotient ring. Restriction of scalars commutes with the chosen open extension and closed pushforward. Apply the normalized finite discrete encoding. Its section-action formula and the constant-function map show that every integral scalar acts as its actual quotient. Transfer the finite constant stratification to ordinary module sheaves and apply constructible etale origin.

source.place: Torsion reduction proof, Lean implementation step 3

proof.text: Apply invariance of finite-type dimension under extension of the residue field to its algebraic closure and the pullback associativity isomorphism. This turns the given geometric fibre bound into the ordinary fibre bound for p.

source.place: Torsion reduction proof, Lean implementation step 4

proof.text: The additive group of the finite coefficient ring is killed by its positive order. Therefore every section of the underlying abelian etale module sheaf is killed by that order, hence the sheaf is torsion. The proper torsion relative cohomological-dimension theorem gives vanishing of its higher direct images in degrees greater than 2d.

source.place: Torsion reduction proof, Lean implementation step 5

proof.text: Properness gives the quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness needed for etale/pro-etale direct-image comparison. Apply comparison to the sheaf in degree zero. Exact comparison commutes with homology and transfers higher direct-image vanishing to Y_proet.

source.place: Torsion reduction proof, Lean implementation step 6

proof.text: Categorical weak contractibility lifts sections of every epimorphism of set sheaves at V. The affine weakly contractible abelian evaluation theorem makes evaluation at V exact. Sections of p_* at V identify with sections on the pullback X times_Y V, via weakly etale localization. This restriction preserves injectives, so derived composition, exact evaluation and compatibility between bounded-below and unbounded derived functors identify the asserted cohomology with evaluation of the vanishing higher direct image.

source.place: Torsion reduction proof, Lean implementation step 7

split_report.summary: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: the isolated imported statement omitted the standing finite-type setting needed for constructibility and retrocompact-complement exactness. Restored that setting explicitly, made condensed integral and finite constant coefficient rings and restriction to X_V explicit, and expanded the original four paragraphs into six steps using existing nodes only. See report.md for the non-quasi-compact-open counterexample and source audit. Replaced the ring-theoretic exact-sections citation by the general categorical evaluation theorem, proving passage to the localized site explicitly; used the exact-derived-functor statement to avoid an uncited injective-resolution existence assertion. Second reading makes the scheme-to-topological Noetherian implication explicit, checks exactness over the integral ring using arbitrary-ring open/closed recollement and the coefficient isomorphism, and supplies the affine-cover and topological-dimension statements needed to pass the ring dimension theorem to scheme fibres. Q152 resumed the retained sandbox, compared it with the current repository (identical at restart), and retained the statement, earlier proof and search history. The long reduction step is now three steps: Noetherian hypotheses, integral exactness/projection formula, and finite constructibility. The finite-presentation transition now cites the existing finite constant cokernel theorem rather than proving a separate comparison inline. All eight steps have verbatim statement citations and a fresh source review in report.md. No new nodes.
